# Provisional Validation Report: Commercial Elevator Predictive Maintenance

**Summary:** Provisional evaluation concludes with a verdict of **NEEDS_WORK** (decision reason: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE) with a composite score of 4.3 and low confidence (0.18). The core value proposition—replacing quarterly inspections with retrofit vibration telemetry—lacks empirical validation on user demand and regulatory viability.

## Scope
- **Startup Idea:** A subscription service fitting retrofit vibration sensors to commercial building lifts to detect bearing wear weeks before breakdown, aiming to replace fixed quarterly inspection contracts.
- **Category:** Commercial Elevator Predictive Maintenance
- **Target User:** Commercial building facilities managers and property operations directors
- **Problem:** Periodic calendar-based lift inspections miss intermediate bearing degradation, resulting in unexpected outages and tenant complaints.
- **Technology Claim:** Non-invasive retrofit vibration sensors paired with anomaly detection algorithms can detect mechanical bearing wear weeks in advance without integrating into proprietary elevator control systems.
- **As of:** 2026-09-06

## Five-Score Rubric
| Dimension | Score | Thin? | Anchor Matched |
|---|---|---|---|
| Demand (D) | 1 / 5 | Yes | Evidence does not reach this question — the sentiment branch returned fewer than 5 usable threads and no problem thread. |
| Market (M) | 2 / 5 | Yes | At least 1 market source names a buyer segment for this problem. |
| Competitive Room (C) | 2 / 5 | Yes | No source states an axis of beatability, and either no competitor is named or at least 1 named competitor is not shown to be vendor owned. |
| Feasibility (F) | 2 / 5 | No | At least 1 repository was returned, and none of them is reusable: none is marked SOLVES_ENTIRELY or PARTIAL, or those that are lack a commercial licence or a push within 12 months. |
| Headroom Over Free (X) | 5 / 5 | No | No free substitute, no free product, and free coverage settled, and every repository marked PARTIAL covers only a separable part of the core job, with at least 1 such repository in the evidence. |

## Verdict & Confidence
- **Verdict:** NEEDS_WORK
- **Decision Reason:** INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
- **Composite Score:** 4.3
- **Confidence:** 0.18 (LOW)
- **Provisional:** True

## Evidence Gaps
- Complete evidence gap in user sentiment: the single search attempt using the query 'elevator predictive maintenance' returned an empty status with 0 results, leaving no problem verification, workaround maintenance data, or payment behavior evidence.
- Statutory jurisdiction requirements specifying mandatory on-site physical elevator inspections regardless of continuous digital monitoring.
- Potential liability and OEM warranty invalidation risks introduced by attaching third-party hardware to certified vertical transportation equipment.
- No identified paying customer segments.

## Risks
What threatens this verdict:
- **Thin Evidence Dimensions:** Demand (D), Market (M), and Competitive Room (C) are all flagged thin, making the assessment vulnerable to new evidence.
- **Failed Tool Branch:** The sentiment branch status returned `empty`, meaning customer pain and willingness to pay remain completely unmeasured.
- **Unmaintained or Non-Commercial Codebases:** Feasibility relies on unmaintained or restricted codebases. [matlab-deep-learning/Industrial-Machinery-Anomaly-Detection](https://github.com/matlab-deep-learning/Industrial-Machinery-Anomaly-Detection) and [aurelienmorgan/abnormal_vibrations_watchdog](https://github.com/aurelienmorgan/abnormal_vibrations_watchdog) lack commercial licenses (60 and 69 months since push respectively). [MatPiech/motor-fault-diagnosis](https://github.com/MatPiech/motor-fault-diagnosis) and [judithspd/predictive-maintenance](https://github.com/judithspd/predictive-maintenance) have commercial licenses but are aged (13 and 63 months since push), while [Ayushkothari96/pulse](https://github.com/Ayushkothari96/pulse) is irrelevant.
- **Incumbent Presence Without Beatability Data:** [OXMaint](https://oxmaint.com/industries/facility-management/connected-elevator-maintenance-iot-monitoring) already advertises IoT monitoring and AI tracking motor health, door cycles, and ride quality, but pricing is unpublished and beatability axes are unverified.
- **Regulatory and Contractual Obstacles:** Statutory requirements may mandate on-site physical inspections, and third-party retrofits risk OEM warranty invalidation.

## Kill Criteria
- Municipal or state building safety regulations mandate quarterly in-person technician inspections with no legal exemption or reduced fee allowed for continuous digital sensor monitoring.
- Major commercial property insurers state elevator coverage will be voided if OEM quarterly physical inspection schedules are replaced by third-party sensor alerts.
- Facilities managers report that existing multi-year full-service OEM elevator maintenance contracts prohibit third-party sensor retrofits or cannot be carved out without financial penalties.

## Cheapest Next Test
Interview 5 commercial property facilities managers to determine whether local elevator safety codes permit replacing physical quarterly inspections with IoT monitoring, or if inspections remain legally mandated regardless of telemetry.

## Sources
- [OXMaint](https://oxmaint.com/industries/facility-management/connected-elevator-maintenance-iot-monitoring): Prevent elevator breakdowns with IoT monitoring and AI. Track ride quality, door cycles & motor health for proactive maintenance alerts.
- [Fortune Business Insights](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/elevator-maintenance-market-113488): The global elevator maintenance market size is projected to grow from $38.33 billion in 2026 to $68.25 billion by 2034, exhibiting a CAGR of 7.50%.
- [iFactory AI](https://ifactoryapp.com/predictive-maintenance/predictive-maintenance-elevators-high-rise-buildings): Explore how predictive maintenance helps maintain elevator systems in high-rise buildings by preventing mechanical failures, reducing downtime, and ensuring reliable service.
- [matlab-deep-learning/Industrial-Machinery-Anomaly-Detection](https://github.com/matlab-deep-learning/Industrial-Machinery-Anomaly-Detection): Industrial-Machinery-Anomaly-Detection (relevance: PARTIAL, license permits commercial: false, months since push: 60).
- [MatPiech/motor-fault-diagnosis](https://github.com/MatPiech/motor-fault-diagnosis): motor-fault-diagnosis (relevance: PARTIAL, license permits commercial: true, months since push: 13).
- [Ayushkothari96/pulse](https://github.com/Ayushkothari96/pulse): pulse (relevance: IRRELEVANT, license permits commercial: true, months since push: 5).
- [judithspd/predictive-maintenance](https://github.com/judithspd/predictive-maintenance): predictive-maintenance (relevance: PARTIAL, license permits commercial: true, months since push: 63).
- [aurelienmorgan/abnormal_vibrations_watchdog](https://github.com/aurelienmorgan/abnormal_vibrations_watchdog): abnormal_vibrations_watchdog (relevance: PARTIAL, license permits commercial: false, months since push: 69).
